overall: The AG found the Commission violated the Open Meeting Law by discussing and voting to release a reasonably anticipated dock RDA not listed on the April 12 notice, ordered future compliance, declined to review the public-participation claim, and ordered no further remedial action.

allegations.summary: Commission discussed and voted to release a dock RDA at 153 Hupi Road at its April 12 meeting, though the topic was not on the posted notice.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the 153 Hupi Road application was reasonably anticipated for discussion at the April 12 meeting.

allegations.summary: Commission limited public participation during its March 8 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: As public participation is discretionary, this allegation, even if true, would not constitute a violation of G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that a similar future violation may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Law.
remedy_passage: We order the Commission’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Commission that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
